segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
were [saying]:
"It is not right to give the poll-tax to Caesar,
and to make mortal lords over us."
And after thirty years,
on Wednesday, the sixth of the latter Kanun (January),
He was baptized in the Jordan by John.
And when our Lord was, in the flesh, two years old,
and Joseph and Mary were going up from Nazareth to Jerusalem,
and they came to Bethlehem,
the Magi came,
and there they worshipped Him.
And on that very night they departed to Egypt.
And they were there two years,
until Herod died,
and then they returned.
Now that Holy Virgin was, when she bore Him, thirteen (fifteen?) years old,
and at fifty-one (sixty-three?) she died.
Concerning the coming of the Magi, Longinus the Roman sage wrote to Caesar:
"Persians from the East have crossed over and entered the territory of your empire,
and have offered gifts to a child who was born in Judah,
who he is, and whose son he is, we have not yet heard."
And Augustus sent word:
"Herod the satrap whom we left there,
he will inform us who he is."
And as for the year of our Lord's birth, although chroniclers have placed it differently,
only that year three hundred and nine of the Greeks we have found to have begun on a Monday, apart from those other [dates] which they recorded.
Now Herod, when he had killed the children of Bethlehem and its borders, the Lord struck him,
and he was tormented for two years,
and died at seventy years of age.
And Augustus appointed Archelaus his son,
who reigned for nine years.
And when he offended,
he was cast into exile to Vienne (Vienna?), a city of the Gauls, of Gaul, that is,
France? {OCR?}.
And then Augustus appointed the four rulers (tetrarchs): Herod, and Antipater, and Philip—
these three were the brothers of Archelaus—
and the fourth, Lysanias, a stranger.
And in that same year Augustus died.
After Augustus Caesar, Tiberius Caesar [reigned] twenty-three years.
And in his fourteenth year, Pilate was sent as governor to the Jews,
and became procurator over them.
And he brought the image of Caesar... {OCR?} [in the year] three hundred and eleven of the Greeks our Lord Jesus the Messiah was born.
To this reckoning we hold fast in this entire history.
